Diary of a Man in Despair ( Tagebuch eines Verzweifelten ) is a journal by the German writer Friedrich Reck-Malleczewen during the 1930s and 1940s, expressing his passionate opposition to Adolf Hitler and Nazism . It was originally published in 1947, but received little recognition. It has since been republished in English and has become regarded as a classic statement about Nazi Germany. The New York Times said the journal is stunning to read because, in it, invective achieves the level of art and hatred achieves a tragic grandeur. [ 1 ]
